Games, concepts, and real-time compositions.

This ensemble is for instrumentalists who want to expand their improvisational voice beyond traditional harmonic and rhythmic structures. Working through guided exercises, structured prompts, and collective compositions in real time, the focus is on the skills that make spontaneous music-making feel connected and alive — deep listening, real-time response, group sound, texture, pacing, form, and discovering new possibilities on your instrument.

Why this course

What you'll work on.

Open Spaces builds on a set of skills you grow over time. The course works through games, concepts, and real-time compositions — guided frameworks that balance openness with clear musical intention.

Over six sessions, you'll work on:

  • Listening and interaction — stronger awareness of the ensemble, responding musically in the moment
  • Texture and sound — tone color, space, repetition, density, silence, extended textures
  • Freedom within structure — guided improvisation frameworks, prompts that balance openness with intention
  • Group form — building beginnings, transitions, momentum, and endings together in real time
  • Personal voice — moving beyond "right notes" into instinct, curiosity, risk-taking, individual sound

Your Teacher

Chris Bates

Bass · Ensemble Coach · Co-Founder

Chris is a vital figure in the Minnesota music scene and a Co-Founder of North Star Jazz Workshops. Raised in a musical household and trained by MN Orchestra bassist James Clute, Chris developed his improvisational skills at the University of Wisconsin Eau Claire, performing with acclaimed artists such as Red Rodney and Donald Harrison. After honing his craft and earning a McKnight Composer's Fellowship with Motion Poets, Chris shifted focus to family life before reemerging fully in 2006 as a composer and performer.

His debut album, New Hope (2012), garnered critical acclaim, followed by notable projects with The Good Vibes Trio and Atlantis Quartet. His compositions have been performed by big bands and new music ensembles like Zeitgeist, and his recent collaborations include soundtracks, live radio dramas, and teaching engagements at the University of Minnesota Morris. Chris continues to push creative boundaries with numerous recordings and performances, maintaining a dynamic presence across various musical genres.

Is this class for you?

A few things to know before signing up.

This is an ensemble course for instrumentalists. You're a good fit if:

  • You're curious about open improvisation, game pieces, and structured spontaneity
  • You're an ensemble player looking to deepen listening and interaction
  • You feel stuck in chord-scale thinking and want to break out
  • You're a creative musician looking to expand your improvisational vocabulary

You don't need prior experience with this kind of playing — just openness, curiosity, and basic comfort on your instrument. If you're not sure whether this is the right fit, email us or book a quick call.
